conviction_note: Two forces of similar size pull opposite ways. (1) H World's own FY2026 revenue guide of +4-8% implies H2 revenue growth of only -2.1% to +5.4% after H1 grew +11%; the company beat the high end of its own guide in Q3 2025, so a beat and another raise are likely. (2) Every China hotel peer that reported Q3 after H World last spoke (Atour, Jinjiang, IHG, Wyndham, Marriott) shows flat-to-negative China RevPAR, and Golden Week RevPAR fell about 2%, so the RevPAR line and the Q4 tone are at risk. Last year's Q3 print had the same shape (beat, cautious Q4) and the stock fell about 5% pre-market. The stock is up about 12% since the last print, short interest is rising, and the consensus bar is disputed. p_up 46 on an abs move of 6.5 gives -0.52. The findings sum to -0.9 for the same reasons; the two measurements agree in sign and roughly in size.

Company guide: no Q3 guide; FY2026 group revenue +4-8% (raised from 2-6%), HWC +7-11%, M&F +16-20%, all from the Q2 release (https://finviz.com/news/382633/h-world-group-limited-reports-second-quarter-and-interim-of-2026-unaudited-financial-results, 2026-08-17). At about 6.8 RMB/USD, $1.08bn is about RMB7.35bn (+5.5% y/y against Q3 2025's RMB6.96bn) and $1.14bn is about RMB7.75bn (+11%). print_vs_bar_pct is measured against the $1.08bn figure.
positioning_check: Short interest 12,185,048 shares at the 2026-10-30 FINRA settlement, about 3.9% of shares outstanding, 7.33 days to cover. It rose for two settlements in a row (+840,598 on 10-15, +776,407 on 10-30). Source: https://equibles.com/stocks/htht/shortinterest, read 2026-11-13. That is moderate, not crowded by the 18-23%-of-float squeeze standard, so the negatives are not shrunk for squeeze risk. The 25-delta skew is null in the baseline. Put/call open interest is 0.42 on only 78 contracts, and the ATM spread is 55% of mid, so the 6.06% event-implied move is indicative only. Tape: spot $50.18, +7.91% over 20 days, -1.68% over 5 days. Earnings Whispers puts the stock up about 12% since the August print while the S&P fell about 5%, and calls sentiment 'modestly bullish' with the Street 'betting on a finish near the high end of guidance'.

findings.finding: H World's FY2026 group revenue guide of +4-8% (raised from 2-6% on 2026-08-17) implies H2 2026 revenue growth of only -2.1% to +5.4%. Arithmetic: FY2025 revenue was RMB25,307m. H1 2026 was RMB13,117m (Q1 5,996 at +11.1%, Q2 7,121 at +10.8%). The guide range is RMB26,319-27,332m, so H2 must be RMB13,202-14,215m against H2 2025's RMB13,486m (Q3 6,961 + Q4 6,525). M&F revenue grew +25% in Q2 against an FY M&F guide of 16-20%. On its last Q3 print (2025) H World beat the high end of its own quarterly revenue guide. Unless something unannounced reverses, Q3 revenue lands above the guide-implied run-rate and the FY revenue guide is raised again. The Street's FY revenue consensus ($3.88bn, near the top of the $3.76-3.91bn USD range) already expects a top-of-range finish, so only a raise ABOVE the current top is new.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-08-17 Q2 print (revenue beat, FY guide raised, $2.5bn 3-year return plan) closed +11.29% on the event day, per the baseline bar for that date. On the 2025-11-17 Q3 print, revenue beat the high end of guide but the Q4 guide of +2-6% disappointed and the stock fell 5.23% pre-market (https://www.itiger.com/hans/news/1157222452; close not verified). So this name pays for raises and sells beats that come with a cautious next-quarter guide.
findings.why_not_priced: The headline FY range is in every preview, but the H2-implied deceleration to roughly +1.6% at the midpoint is not, and the previews disagree on the Q3 revenue bar ($1.05bn, $1.08bn and $1.14bn). If the market had worked through the arithmetic, the previews would quote one bar and frame a raise as the base case. Instead Earnings Whispers stresses 'tougher second-half comparisons'. FY consensus near the top of the range means part of this is priced, so the size is small.
findings.independence: FY2025 revenue of RMB25.307bn: https://www.itiger.com/news/1140724402 (2026-03). Q1 2026 revenue of RMB5,996m, +11.1%: https://uk.marketscreener.com/news/h-world-group-limited-reports-earnings-results-for-the-first-quarter-ended-march-31-2026-ce7f5bd2d189f024. Q3 2025 beat its guide's high end: https://www.itiger.com/hans/news/1157222452. Q2 2026 beat consensus ($1.05bn against $982.8m, Benzinga figures quoted in search). All are company numbers; the arithmetic is mine.

findings.finding: Atour (ATAT), the nearest listed China midscale peer, reported Q3 2026 on 2026-11-10, after H World last spoke. Its same-hotel RevPAR (hotels open more than 18 months) fell 4.2% y/y (RMB356.6 against 372.2), worse than its Q2 2026 same-hotel figure of about -3%. Same-hotel occupancy was 79.5% against 81.1%, and same-hotel ADR fell to RMB433.7 from 443.1. Blended RevPAR was about flat (+0.5%), propped up by new hotels. H World's Q2 2026 same-hotel RevPAR was -3.0% with blended +1.1%, so the read-across points to H World's Q3 same-hotel RevPAR at -3% to -5% and blended RevPAR flat to negative, below Goldman's 2026-10-26 view that H World room revenue would be steady to slightly up.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the 2025-11-17 print, same-hotel RevPAR of -4.7% came with the -5.23% pre-market move, which commentary attributed mainly to the Q4 guide (https://www.itiger.com/hans/news/1157222452). Atour itself fell about 6.1% after its Q2 2026 print on mature-hotel RevPAR deceleration, per a search summary of https://www.webull.com/news/15483307382096896.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a peer's number, public for three trading days, and HTHT fell 1.68% over the last 5 sessions, so it is partly priced. The Earnings Whispers preview of 2026-11-09, written before Atour reported, still frames China ADR as having had 'four straight positive readings'. If the market had fully priced a deteriorating same-hotel trend, HTHT would not be within 2% of its post-earnings high.
findings.independence: This is a proxy, not H World's own number. Atour is upper-midscale while H World's base is economy/midscale. Q2 2026 Atour same-hotel at 97.0% of the prior year: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/atour-lifestyle-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-20/ (search summary). Same direction from global chains, a different source: IHG Greater China Q3 RevPAR -3.3%, Wyndham China -10%, Marriott Greater China about flat (https://www.cnfin.com/hg-lb/detail/20261028/4487532_1.html, 2026-10-28; https://finviz.com/news/413000/marriott-international-reports-third-quarter-2026-results).

findings.finding: Jinjiang Hotels, the closest economy/midscale peer to H World's Hanting/JI base, reported Q3 2026 domestic limited-service RevPAR of RMB167.13, -2.23% y/y. That is about the same as its implied Q2 2026 rate (Q1 +3.68%, H1 +0.5%, so Q2 is about -2.5%), and Yicai cites domestic same-store RevPAR down about 3% over the first three quarters. This says the economy-segment level is negative but did not deteriorate from Q2 to Q3. That partly offsets the Atour read and points to H World's same-hotel RevPAR holding near its Q2 -3%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: H World's RevPAR prints: Q1 2026 RevPAR +3.0% (best since 2024) came with a reported -2.5% after-hours move on a slight EPS miss (weakly sourced). Q2 2026 RevPAR +1.1% with a guide raise and a return plan closed +11.3%. RevPAR has not been the line this stock traded on in 2026; guidance and capital return have.
findings.why_not_priced: It was published 2026-10-30/11-02 in Chinese broker notes (Soochow, Guojin) and Yicai, and the A-share figures are not quoted in the English previews. A level of about -2% is consistent with what the Street already models (Goldman: Jinjiang about -2%), so it is mostly priced. The new part is only the absence of Q2-to-Q3 deterioration.
findings.independence: The Q3 -2.23% figure comes from Soochow Securities via search summary (https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H3_AP202610311831278894_1.pdf, Guojin 2026-10-31, text not extractable). H1 figures: https://m.gelonghui.com/news/5301562. It is a proxy and shares the 'China Q3 RevPAR soft' theme with the Atour finding, but points to a different trend (stable rather than worsening), so it is filed separately with a smaller size.

findings.finding: Q4 and forward-tone risk: Yicai's grassroots survey (2026-10-08) put 2026 National Day Golden Week hotel RevPAR down about 2% y/y on lower occupancy. Cross-regional trips were up only 0.7%, and the survey expects Q4 RevPAR roughly flat. A Haitong view quoted in search expects Q4 RevPAR declines and 2027 supply pressure. H World's FY RevPAR guide is still 'slight increase' (YTD about Q1 +3.0%, Q2 +1.1%, Q3 likely about 0), and its Q4 2025 comp was positive. The print therefore risks a cautious Q4 tone or a trim of the RevPAR outlook, the line that sank the Q3 2025 print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-11-17: Q3 beat with Q4 revenue guided +2-6%, and the stock fell 5.23% pre-market on 'Q4 guidance disappoints' (https://www.itiger.com/hans/news/1157222452).
findings.why_not_priced: Golden Week data is public, but the stock rose about 12% after the August print and sits near highs, so the market leans on the guide raise and the capital return rather than on Q4 RevPAR. If the Q4 risk were priced, the stock would have de-rated after Golden Week. It did not; it is +7.9% over 20 days.
findings.independence: This is a proxy (a grassroots survey, not H World data). Industry Q3 weakness in Greater China across IHG, Wyndham and Marriott: https://www.cnfin.com/hg-lb/detail/20261028/4487532_1.html. Shares the 'China RevPAR soft' theme with the Atour finding but lands on Q4 and guidance rather than the reported quarter.

findings.finding: H World opened 1,035 hotels gross in H1 2026, 20% below H1 2025 (Morgan Stanley's question on the Q2 call), and CLSA put China net openings down 29% y/y. The FY gross opening target of 2,200-2,300 was maintained, which requires about 1,165-1,265 openings in H2, an acceleration of more than 10% over H1. Q3 openings and any change to the target are disclosed at the print. A cut would hit the M&F growth story that justifies the multiple.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean isolated reaction to the openings line found. The pipeline (3,054 HWC hotels, up y/y and q/q) was cited as offsetting on the Q2 call.
findings.why_not_priced: Management reaffirmed the target in August and previews do not mention the H2 acceleration required. If the market doubted the target, previews would flag openings as the risk line. Earnings Whispers mentions the 20% shortfall only as background. The pipeline growth is a real offset, so the size is small.
findings.independence: CLSA (2026-09-01) China net openings -29% y/y, via search summary of https://m.gelonghui.com/news/5304087. Q2 release: 498 openings in the quarter, 497 of them asset-light (https://pulse2.com/h-world-manachised-and-franchised-revenue-jumps-25-as-497-of-498-china-openings-use-asset-light-model/). Same company documents as finding 1, a different line.

findings.finding: The $2.5bn three-year shareholder return plan (effective 2026-08-17; about $833m a year, about 5% of a roughly $15.5bn market cap) means the Q3 print will carry the first quarter of buyback execution under the new plan. The $275m dividend was paid in September. Visible execution, or any acceleration or special payout, supports the stock.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The plan's announcement came with the +11.3% move on 2026-08-17, together with the guide raise.
findings.why_not_priced: The plan is announced and in the wire, so it is mostly priced. Only the pace of execution is unknown: no October or November HKEX buyback returns were found, which suggests limited open-market buying so far and makes acceleration a small upside optionality.
findings.independence: Same document as finding 1. CostAR on the plan: https://www.costar.com/article/1857661371/h-world-raises-outlook-and-approves-2-5-billion-shareholder-return.

findings.finding: AAII (I/B/E/S data, 2026-11-13) shows the next-quarter EPS consensus at $0.84 from 2 analysts, with 1 downgrade and 0 upgrades in the past month and an Estimate Revisions Score of 38 ('Negative'). findings.why_not_priced: It is a two-analyst I/B/E/S cut not quoted in the previews. The page mislabels the quarter (Q2 actuals shown as Q3), so the mapping of the $0.84 to Q3 is uncertain and the size is small.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers EPS bar of $0.75 (2026-11-09) against Benzinga's $0.78 shows the bar is not unified. No direct second source for the downgrade.

baseline_tension: The skew is unavailable and the option market is thin (78 contracts OI, 55% spread). The +7.9% 20-day run-up and the price near highs cut against a positive read on the expected guide raise. The peer RevPAR evidence agrees with a pullback risk, so I lean slightly negative (p_up 46) rather than following the guide arithmetic.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar disputed: three revenue consensus figures $1.05-1.14bn and two EPS figures): the guide-arithmetic finding was capped from +1.5 to +1.0

Lesson 5 (a proxy is filed smaller): the Golden Week grassroots-survey finding was trimmed from -1.0 to -0.8. The Atour peer print was kept at -0.8 because it is a counterparty-class print landing after the company last spoke
Lesson 7: short interest was checked (3.9% of SO, 7.3 days to cover, rising); not crowded, so the negatives were not shrunk further

Lesson on an untrustworthy reaction history: the base rate was rebuilt from confirmed prints (Aug 2026 +11.3%, Nov 2025 about -5% pre-market), and abs_move stays at 6.5 rather than the baseline's median of 1.8
